rules.statement: In pre-release code with no shipped consumers, make the change as a clean cutover (rename, move, remove or change signatures directly) instead of adding compatibility shims, obsolete aliases or duplicate settings that keep the old shape.
rules.why: Nothing has shipped, so there is no backward compatibility to keep. The best long-term, cohesive design is preferred over a minimal patch that preserves compatibility, and PublicAPI churn is expected.
rules.check: Look for [Obsolete] forwarding members, old-name setting aliases, adapter overloads or 'kept for compatibility' comments added in a pre-release package.

rules.statement: Model an extensible vocabulary (settings, scopes, profiles, grant types, client-authentication methods, claims, stores, endpoints and similar) as string names plus registered descriptors or strategies, and use an enum, a switch over its members or a hard-coded relationship between them only when the set is provably closed.
rules.why: Consumers and sibling packages must be able to add a member by registering it, without editing the library. A closed construct blocks that.
rules.check: Look for a new enum, a switch/if-chain over vocabulary values, or hard-coded member relationships where another package could plausibly need an extra member, with no justification that the set is closed.

rules.statement: Use authorization code with PKCE `S256` for interactive clients, and do not add or enable the implicit flow, hybrid flows that return tokens in the front channel, or the resource-owner password flow.
rules.why: Current guidance (the OAuth 2.1 direction, RFC 9700 Security BCP) treats these as the modern secure defaults. The repository should follow them without asking.
rules.check: Look for implicit/hybrid/password grant support, PKCE made optional, or the `plain` code challenge method being allowed.

rules.statement: Sign tokens with asymmetric algorithms such as `PS256` or `ES256`, and never use `HS256` or other shared-secret signing for tokens that cross a trust boundary.
rules.why: Modern recommended practice requires asymmetric signing across trust boundaries.
rules.check: Look for HS256/HMAC signing defaults or configuration for issued ID/access tokens consumed by other parties.

rules.statement: Validate redirect URIs by exact match against registered values, never by prefix, wildcard or pattern matching.
rules.why: Exact-match redirect URIs are required by the Security BCP and OAuth 2.1.
rules.check: Look for StartsWith, Contains, regex, wildcard or case-insensitive comparisons of redirect URIs.

rules.statement: Default issued tokens to short lifetimes and sender-constraining where applicable, grant least-privilege scopes, and ship secure-by-default headers and CORS settings.
rules.why: These are the modern recommended identity-platform defaults the repository adopts without asking.
rules.check: Look for long default token lifetimes, broad default scopes, permissive CORS (any origin with credentials) or missing security headers in defaults.

rules.statement: When a change fixes an insecure or outdated design, update the surrounding code comments, docs and decision records in the same change so that none of them still describe the old shape.
rules.why: Existing code and docs are point-in-time artifacts. The repository, not chat history, must carry the correction.
rules.check: Look for a design change whose diff leaves comments, XML docs, markdown docs or ADRs that still describe the previous behavior.

rules.statement: When pinning a tool, package, provider or action version, pin the latest release from its upstream release feed or registry, not a locally installed or remembered version.
rules.why: A locally installed or remembered version says nothing about what is current upstream.
rules.check: Look for newly added or bumped version pins that are older than the current upstream release.

rules.statement: Never put agent attribution in a commit message: no `Co-authored-by:` trailer naming an agent or bot identity, no `Claude-Session:` trailer and no 'Generated with' line.
rules.why: A commit records the people who wrote it. The host lists the agent in the contributor graph, and undoing that means rewriting published history.
rules.check: Look in commit messages and PR descriptions for agent co-author trailers, session trailers or generated-with lines.

rules.statement: Add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` in the same pull request for every consumer-visible change.
rules.why: Durable knowledge, including consumer-visible changes, must live in versioned repository content.
rules.check: Look for public API, behavior or configuration changes with no matching CHANGELOG.md update in the diff.

rules.statement: Track deferred work and follow-ups as GitHub issues and reference them by issue number, not as untracked TODO notes or 'remaining' bullets left in docs, and close completed issues from the pull request with `Closes #<number>`.
rules.why: GitHub issues are the single source of truth for pending work, and an item must never be both done and still framed as pending.
rules.check: Look for new TODO/remaining/follow-up notes with no issue reference, or a PR that completes work but leaves 'still open' bullets or lacks a Closes reference.

rules.statement: When adding a file that a root build file imports, also re-admit it in `.dockerignore` so the container image build can see it.
rules.why: The local gate does not build the host image, so only the Host image check on the PR catches the missing file.
rules.check: Look for a new file imported by Directory.Build.props/targets or similar root build files with no matching `.dockerignore` re-admit entry.
